dateline: Santiago, Chile — November 1970–March 1990 | Accountability under threat, August 2026
heroHeadline: Chile Faces First-Ever IACHR Hearing as Kast Moves to Strip Human Rights Institute's Legal Powers
heroSubtitle: Justice Minister Rabat unveiled a bill stripping the INDH's power to file criminal complaints, calling the institute 'left-wing tinted,' as the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights held its first hearing on Kast-era rollbacks — citing 'passive pardons' behind the release of convicted rights violators. The reckoning came days after DNA confirmed a woman listed as disappeared since 1973 is alive in Argentina, and after the last fugitive convicted in Víctor Jara's murder was captured.
footerNote: Data sourced from Valech Report, Rettig Commission, Vicaría de la Solidaridad, US FOIA declassified documents, Chilean Archivo Nacional, and ongoing judicial proceedings
